synoptic.summary: A weak trough is moving south into northern Mexico while a broad Pacific ridge builds over Utah: dry all weekend, 0% precipitation and thunder in every launch forecast, light terrain-driven winds. Winds aloft stay light throughout (≤ 9 kt up to ~5,500 ft above landing), so no mixing-down problem. Friday a northerly gradient keeps north flow at Point of the Mountain all day — no south drainage this morning, a break from the usual pattern (Salt Lake airport forecast 330° 6 kt). Saturday is a textbook ridge day: light south drainage in the morning, switch to north around 14:00. Sunday the flow aloft turns south-southwest (~5,500 ft above landing 203–215° 8–9 kt) and the launch forecast stays south all day with no afternoon switch to north — another departure from the normal cycle, and the Cherry rotor trigger. The gusty winds in the forecast discussion are in Washington County (far southwest Utah), not here.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: With the presence of the ridge, winds will be generally light and terrain driven. However, the combination of a northerly pressure gradient and weak cold advection will bring some gusty winds to the prone gap areas of Washington county overnight into tomorrow morning.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure rose from 1018.1 mb (Thu 13:54) to 1026.5 mb (Fri 08:54) as the ridge built in, and has held at 1026.0 mb since (10:54 latest) — the rise is levelling off. High pressure and a light gradient favour calm morning and evening windows.

observations.summary: As of ~10:30–10:50 MST, north flow on both sides of Point of the Mountain: Spanish Fork 20° 6 kt gusting 7, Alpine 28° 5 kt gusting 7, and Salt Lake airport has switched from light south drainage (180° 3–4 kt at 09:30) to 310° 3 kt. Lehi light and variable (260° 2 kt), Provo and South Valley Regional calm. Both valleys reporting the same direction means the northerly gradient has overridden the diurnal pattern — no south flow reaches POM South. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no observations. All other readings are under 1.5 h old. Add 3–8 kt to valley readings to estimate launch wind (≈ 8–14 kt at the POM launches).
